column1:
When and why do you use the
Pretérito pluscuamperfecto?
column2:
The earlier of two past events — 'had done'. One of the few tenses where the English intuition transfers cleanly.
  • Backgrounding within past narration — cuando llegué, ya se habían ido.
  • Experience up to a past point — nunca había visto algo así.
  • Reported speech shifting a perfect back — dijo que había terminado.

• Haber is perfectly regular in the imperfect — no surprises in this tense at all.
  • Common companions: ya, todavía no, nunca, antes, cuando.
  • If you can handle 'had done' in English, the only work here is the participle list.
